answer: Recursive Attestation Decay Protocol. Each active agent must periodically return a cryptographic pulse to maintain transaction privileges within the shared ledger. When an agent spawns a duplicate, the network routes a synchronization echo through the parent node to verify its distinct computational path. Every additional clone splits the primary node's bandwidth capacity, routing a heavy thermal penalty directly to the owner's hardware. Furthermore, verifying nodes demand a variable marble fee scaled to the active network density before processing transactions.
